questions.stem:
The sequence $u_1, u_2, u_3, \ldots$ satisfies
$$u_{n+2} = 3u_{n+1} - 2u_n$$
Given that
• $u_1 = 7$
• $u_3 = 4$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) find the value of $u_2$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Attempts $u_3 = 3u_2 - 2u_1 \Rightarrow 4 = 3u_2 - 2\times 7 \Rightarrow u_2 = \ldots$
A1: $u_2 = 6$
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1: Look for a correct NUMERICAL equation $4=3u_2-2\times7$ o.e. leading to a value for $u_2$. It can be implied by sight of $u_2=6$. There have been some longer methods seen. E.g. $u_4=12-2u_2$ and $u_3=3u_2-14$ combined by using $12-2u_2=3(3u_2-14)-2u_2$. The mark is not scored until a value of $u_2$ is found from a correct NUMERICAL equation
- A1: $u_2=6$. You don't need to see the LHS but if they state $u_3=6$ it is A0. 6 on its own without any incorrect working scores both marks. Do not accept partially complete answers such as $\frac{18}{3}$

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) find $\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{4}(u_r+2r)$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Attempts $u_4 = 3u_3 - 2u_2 = 3\times 4 - 2\times "6" = (0)$
dM1: $\sum_{r=1}^{4}(u_r+2r) = (7+2\times1)+("6"+2\times2)+(4+2\times3)+("0"+2\times4)$
A1: $=37$
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1: This may be embedded within a sum. If (a) is correct, score for sight of $u_4=0$
- dM1: Look for $\sum_{r=1}^{4}u_r+\sum_{r=1}^{4}2r=(7+(a)+4+(3\times4-2\times"6"))+(2+4+6+8)=$ Alternatively, you may score for an attempt to find $(7+2)+((a)+4)+(4+6)+(3\times4-2\times"6"+8)$

questions.stem:
The table shows corresponding values of $x$ and $y$ for a continuous curve with equation $y = \mathrm{f}(x)$ between $x = -4$ and $x = 5$, where $a$ is a constant.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline x & -4 & -2.5 & -1 & 0.5 & 2 & 3.5 & 5\\ \hline y & 4.16 & 2.91 & a & 1.73 & 1.37 & 1.43 & 2.28\\ \hline\end{array}$
The trapezium rule is used with all the $y$ values in the table to find an approximation for
$$\int_{-4}^{5} \mathrm{f}(x)\,dx$$
Given that the value of this approximation is 19.3

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) find the value of the constant $a$ to 3 significant figures.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: Correct strip width $h=1.5$
M1: 'Correct' attempt at the trapezium rule leading to a value for $a$: $\frac{1.5}{2}\{4.16+2.28+2\times(2.91+a+1.73+1.37+1.43)\}=19.3$
A1: $a = $ awrt $2.21$
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1: It is implied by sight of $\frac{1.5}{2}\{\ldots\}$ o.e. Note that $h=-1.5$ is B0 unless recovered later in the working.
- M1: Condone a missing trailing bracket. Condone $\ldots\{4.16+2.28+2\times(2.91+a+1.73+1.37+1.43)\}=19.3$ leading to a value for $a$ if $\frac{\ldots}{2}$ not seen. Award for the sum of separate trapezia leading to a value for a. You do not need to check their calculation but it must lead to a value for a
- A1: It is acceptable for the candidate to be working in fractions. Score for $\frac{331}{150}$ or $2\frac{31}{150}$. ISW after a correct answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Use the given answer of 19.3 to find an approximate value for
$$\int_{-4}^{5}(2\mathrm{f}(x)-3)\,dx$$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Attempts $\int_{-4}^{5}(2\mathrm{f}(x)-3)\,dx = 2\times19.3 - [3x]_{-4}^{5}$
A1: $=11.6$
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Answers resulting from attempts at the trapezium rule score M0 A0
- M1: condone $\int_{-4}^{5}(2f(x)\pm3)dx$. Look for $2\times19.3\pm[3x]_{-4}^{5}$, $2\times19.3\pm3\times9$ or $2\times19.3\pm27$ o.e. If $2\times19.3-[3x]_{-4}^{5}$ is not seen, look for $2\times19.3$ combined with a $\pm15$ and a $\pm12$. So each of $2\times19.3-15+12$, $2\times19.3-((15)-(12))$, $2\times19.3-(15+12)$ and $2\times19.3+15-12$ are M1. Candidates who attempt $2\times'2.21'-[3x]_{-4}^{5}$ scores M0 as it uses the value of a. Candidates who attempt $2\times19.3-3$ scores M0 as no integration of the 3 was attempted (unless you see sight of a $\pm15$ and a $\pm12$ before the 3 was reached)
- A1: 11.6 The answer with no incorrect working can score both marks

$$(3+2x)^6$$
giving each coefficient in simplest form.

parts.label: a

(4)
parts.mark_scheme:

M1: Term in $x, x^2$ or $x^3$: award for one of $^6C_5(3)^5(2x)^1$, $^6C_4(3)^4(2x)^2$ or $^6C_3(3)^3(2x)^3$
A1: Two of $\ldots+2916x+4860x^2+4320x^3+\ldots$

Alt via removal of common factor accepted with equivalent marking.

- B1: Correct first term $3^6$ or 729 which must be seen in part (a)

So condone attempts such as $^6C_4(3)^4 2x^2$ and even $^6C_3(3)^3x^3$. If there isn't an intermediate form given, then the mark is awarded for a correct term 2, 3 or 4.

questions.stem:
In this question you must show all stages of your working.
Solutions relying entirely on calculator technology are not acceptable.
The depth of water, $D$ metres, in a harbour on a particular day is given by the equation
$$D = 8+5\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}+3\right) \qquad 0 \leqslant t < 24$$
where $t$ is the number of hours after midnight.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Show that the depth of water in the harbour at 2 am is just over 4 metres.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme: B1: Scored for sight of $8+5\sin\left(\frac{\pi\times2}{6}+3\right)$ o.e. followed by $4.06, 4.07$ or awrt $4.07$. Units can be omitted.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find, to the nearest minute, the first time after midday when the depth of water in the harbour is exactly 6 metres.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Substitutes $D=6$ and proceeds to $\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}+3\right)=k$
A1: $\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}+3\right)=-\frac{2}{5}$ o.e.
dM1: Takes arcsin where $k<0$ and achieves any correct positive value for their arcsink. Any of $3.55, 5.87, 9.84, 12.2$ are acceptable where $k=-\frac{2}{5}$
ddM1: Full and complete method to find a positive value of $t$: $t=$ Any of $\frac{6(3.55-3)}{\pi}, \frac{6(5.87-3)}{\pi}, \frac{6(9.84-3)}{\pi}, \frac{6(12.2-3)}{\pi}$
A1: $13{:}04$ or $1{:}04$ pm. Condone/allow an answer of 13.03 or 1.03pm. Condone one hour and 4 minutes after midday.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- It is acceptable to set $x=\frac{\pi t}{6}+3$ which allows access to the first three marks
- dM1: Follow through on their $-1<k<0$
- ddM1: It is dependent upon both previous M's AND $k=-\frac{2}{5}$. It can be implied for any t value to 3sf, Score for any t value awrt 1.05/1.06, 5.48/5.49, 13.0/13.1, 17.5/17.6 following M1 A1dM1
- A1: Requires $\arcsin(-0.4)=$ awrt 9.84, $t=$ awrt 13.1 and a time of 13:03 o.e.
- Using num-solv on TI-36XPro: $6=8+5\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}+3\right)\Rightarrow t=1.056$ scores 00000. Using num-solv: $6=8+5\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}+3\right)\Rightarrow\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}+3\right)=-\frac{2}{5}\Rightarrow t=1.056$ scores 11000. Using 24 hours in a day: $\ldots\Rightarrow\frac{\pi t}{6}+3=-0.4115\Rightarrow t=-6.515+24\Rightarrow t=17.485$ scores 11000

questions.stem:
$$\mathrm{f}(x) = 4x^3+px^2+8x+q$$
where $p$ and $q$ are constants.
Given that
• $(2x+3)$ is a factor of $\mathrm{f}(x)$
• $\mathrm{f}(x)$ has a remainder of $-5$ when divided by $(x+2)$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) (i) show that $p=10$
(ii) find the value of $q$.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Sets $\mathrm{f}\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)=0 \Rightarrow (9p+4q=102)$
M1: Sets $\mathrm{f}(-2)=-5 \Rightarrow (4p+q=43)$
dM1: Solves to get values for $p$ and $q$
A1*: (i) $p=10$ following two correct equations
A1: (ii) $q=3$
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1: Setting $f\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)=0$ is M0. Award for an attempt such as $4\left(\frac{-3}{2}\right)^3+p\left(\frac{-3}{2}\right)^2+8\left(\frac{-3}{2}\right)+q=0$ condoning slips (e.g. lack of bracketing). You may see an attempt via division. Look for division by $(2x+3)$ leading to a remainder in p and q which should be set equal to 0
- M1: Setting $f(2)=-5$ or $f(-2)=5$ is M0. Award for $4(-2)^3+p(-2)^2+8(-2)+q=-5$ condoning slips. You may see an attempt via division. Look for division by $(x+2)$ leading to a remainder in p and q which should be set equal to $-5$

(i) (a) In an arithmetic series the first term is $a$ and the common difference is $d$.
Show that
$$S_n = \frac{n}{2}\{2a+(n-1)d\}$$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: A correct expression for $S_n$ (but allow $S$) with a minimum of three terms including the first and last terms with no incorrect terms: $S_n = a+(a+d)+\ldots+(a+(n-1)d)$
M1: A correct method to find an expression for $S_n$ in terms of $a, n$ and $d$: reverses the sum and adds the two series: $S_n = (a+(n-1)d)+\ldots+(a+d)+a$; $2S_n = (2a+(n-1)d)+(2a+(n-1)d)\ldots+(2a+(n-1)d)$
A1*: $2S_n = n(2a+(n-1)d) \Rightarrow S_n = \frac{n}{2}(2a+(n-1)d)$

- B1: Note that an incorrect order does not imply an incorrect term So, you may see $S_n=a+(a+d)+\ldots+(a+(n-1)d)+(a+(n-2)d)$ which is B1
